rationale: Four evaluated points all cluster at 157.05-157.59us with identical 34.603MB simulator DRAM traffic, so the analytic serpentine reuse/traffic hypothesis has not materialized (swizzle=8 and swizzle=16 at the same tile/stages produce identical latency and traffic; swizzle is non-discriminating in this workload). Attempt-00 (128x64x64, stages=1, swizzle=0) remains the incumbent best at 157.05us; attempts 01-03 with block_M=32, stages=3 and varying swizzle are all marginally slower at 157.59us. Domains stay broad: block_M [32,64,128] all divide M=128, block_N [64,128] divide N=4096, block_K [32,64] divide K=4096, stages [1,2,3], swizzle [0,4,8,16]; only four tuples excluded and the 32768-byte portability cap still admits many combos (tightest BM=128,BN=128,BK=64,stages=2). I lower footprint weight from 1 to 0.5 because smem footprint (30720-32768B) has shown no correlation with latency across the observed points, so it should not drive selection away from the incumbent's small block_M=128 neighborhood; pipeline weight reset to 1 since stage-1 was best and deeper pipelining is unvalidated as a benefit. Traffic stays at 1 but is not raised given flat simulator traffic. Next hypothesis: probe untested block_M=64 and block_M=128 with block_K=32/stages=2-3 and block_N=128 combinations to see whether the 157us plateau breaks; if latency remains flat, the tall-skinny M=128 shape is likely saturating and only block_M/tile-count effects remain. Proxy cost is dimensionless ranking only, never microseconds; Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR but not the CUDA binary, and GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality is claimed.
